import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Factorial distance to nearest square

The sequence is defined as
$$a(n) =
\mathrm{round}\left(\frac{\mathrm{round}(\sqrt{n!})}{\left|(\mathrm{round}(\sqrt{n!}))^2 -
n!\right|}\right)$$
for $n \ge 2$.

*References:*
- [A145355](https://oeis.org/A145355)
-/

namespace OeisA145355

open Real

/-- The sequence $a(n) = \mathrm{round}(\mathrm{round}(\sqrt{n!})/|(\mathrm{round}(\sqrt{n!}))^2 - n!|)$. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let fact_r : ℝ := Nat.cast (Nat.factorial n)
  let r_int : ℤ := round (sqrt fact_r)
  let r_real : ℝ := Int.cast r_int
  let den_val : ℝ := abs (r_real ^ 2 - fact_r)
  (round (r_real / den_val)).toNat

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by
  delta a
  norm_num [((Int.floor_eq_iff.mpr _) : _ = (1 : ℤ)), ← not_lt, false, round_eq, Real.sqrt_lt',
    ← lt_sub_iff_add_lt]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 1 := by
  delta a
  norm_num only [Nat.factorial, round_eq, ((Int.floor_eq_iff.2 _) : _ = (2 : ℤ)), Int.toNat,
    ← not_lt, true, abs_of_neg, ← lt_sub_iff_add_lt, Real.sqrt_lt, and_self_iff]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 5 := by
  delta a
  norm_num [Int.toNat, show round (sqrt 24) = 5 by
    norm_num only [← not_lt, false, round_eq, true, Real.sqrt_lt', Int.floor_eq_iff,
      ← lt_sub_iff_add_lt, and_self], round_eq, false, Nat.factorial]

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 5. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 11 := by
  delta a
  norm_num [((Int.floor_eq_iff.2 _) : _ = (11 : ℤ)), round_eq, ← not_lt, Int.toNat,
    ← lt_sub_iff_add_lt, Real.sqrt_lt]

/--
This sequence suggests that the distance between a factorial and the closest power is
tightly bounded.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → a n ≤ C := by
  sorry

end OeisA145355

findings.description: The theorem interprets “the distance between a factorial and the closest power is tightly bounded” as the precise assertion `∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ 2, a n ≤ C`. Writing rₙ = round(√(n!)) and Dₙ = |rₙ² − n!|, this requires Dₙ > rₙ/(C + 1/2): a uniform positive lower bound on the normalized square-distance. OEIS does not explicitly conjecture boundedness of a(n) or specify this quantitative bound. Its three explicit conjectures instead exclude particular factorial-plus-polynomial/prime representations, and the Lean assertion is not an equivalent formulation of those. The qualitative remark might have been intended this way, so this is a source-interpretation concern, not a claim that the theorem is demonstrably false.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A145355, comments, revision #19 (2025-08-18), read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A145/A145355.seq: “This sequence suggests that the distance between a factorial and the closest power is tightly bounded.” It then says the sequence was generated in response to three Povolotsky conjectures: n! + n² ≠ m² apart from n=0, m=1; n! + Σ_{j=1}^n j² ≠ m²; and n! + prime(n) ≠ m^k. No uniform bound on the sequence is stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Supply a reference explicitly supporting uniform boundedness of this sequence and explain the normalized-distance interpretation. Otherwise, formalize one or more of the explicitly stated Diophantine conjectures instead; for example, the first is `∀ n m : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n.factorial + n ^ 2 ≠ m ^ 2`. Do not infer a specific quantitative conjecture solely from “tightly bounded.”

reformulations.difference: Lean uses round(√(n!)) in the numerator, agreeing with the OEIS PARI program and numerical table. The literal OEIS title instead has an unrounded square root in the numerator and a redundant outer round. These formulas differ at n=11: Lean/program/table give 20, while the literal title gives 19. This source-internal discrepancy does not change any assertion made about the sequence in this file.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n≥2, the common denominator D is a positive integer. Since |√(n!) − round(√(n!))| ≤ 1/2, the two unrounded ratios differ by at most 1/2, and their rounded natural-number values differ by at most 1. Consequently, a bound C for either sequence yields a bound C+1 for the other. The four tested values at n=2,3,4,5 also agree. The inequalities in both directions and the equivalence of the two boundedness statements were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. Thus the parenthesization discrepancy is not an independent misformalization; the PARI program and table additionally support Lean’s chosen definition directly.

OEIS supplies no quantified formulation or link to the original discussion; attempts to locate that discussion did not resolve the ambiguity.
review.notes: Checked all six declarations. Exact-arithmetic evaluation agrees with all 9,999 OEIS table entries for n=2,…,10000. The four existing tests have no sorry dependency. Additional Lean checks establish a(0)=a(1)=0, nonnegativity before `Int.toNat`, and sample values including a(11)=20. A separate sorry-free proof uses Bertrand’s postulate to show n! is not a square for n≥2, so division by zero cannot occur in the conjecture’s domain. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, compute.lean, semantics.lean, and equivalence.lean. The ordinary OEIS page was blocked by Cloudflare; the complete public data mirror and linked table were accessible. No source-reported resolution or stale-status issue was found.
